title: 'Flock Flocked up'

reading.body:
This is a case of an automated licence plate reader returning a false match that was treated as a confirmed hit. The failure happened at the point where a camera alert entered a live police deployment, before any officer had verified it against the vehicle in front of them. The system's output was a plate number, and the plate number was wrong.

The mismatch was visible in the alert itself. The camera image showed a Chevy Malibu while the plate belonged to a red Dodge Ram pickup, so the error was catchable by comparing the flagged vehicle description against the vehicle being stopped. Catching it would have required a human check at the roadside, and the facts do not show that one was made before officers drew weapons and made the stop.

What is not established is whether the misread was a known limitation of the system, whether officers were trained to verify alerts before acting, or whether any policy required it. The department's own investigation found no wrongdoing in the K-9 use, and charges against the driver were later dropped, but neither outcome establishes what the camera system did or failed to do.

reports.title: Body cam of TPD officers releasing K-9 on man during traffic stop
Man speaks out after police release K-9 on him during traffic stop: 'Traumatized'
TPD investigation finds no wrongdoing in use of K-9 on man during traffic stop
Charges dropped against man Toledo Police released K-9 on during traffic stop, lawyer says

summary:
Body camera footage was released showing Toledo Police officers releasing a K-9 on a driver during a traffic stop. Officers had received a FLOCK camera alert about a stolen license plate, but the alert was incorrect. The camera image matched a Chevy Malibu while the plate was actually on a red Dodge Ram pickup. The driver, Brandon Upchurch, was stopped, ordered out at gunpoint, and arrested on charges of resisting arrest and obstruction. He received medical attention at the scene.

Officers later realized the plate information was a misread and was not stolen. Multiple TPD officers are under investigation over the incident. Police said they believed the driver might flee and did not know if he or the passenger had weapons. Under TPD's K-9 policy, handlers must weigh the severity of the crime, whether the suspect poses an immediate threat, and whether the suspect is resisting or trying to evade arrest.
